items.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
items.excerpt: After backlash, Meta revised its upcoming business terms (effective Oct 30) to remove language experts said would let it scrape publishers' sites, including news sites, to train its AI.

items.title: Legal experts warn Meta's new terms still grant broad scraping permissions, despite language changes
items.excerpt: Meta removed the word 'train' from its business-account terms after Nieman Lab's report, but legal experts say the revised terms still permit broad scraping of sites 'associated with' business accounts. (published time from RSS pubDate; page Cloudflare-blocked)

items.title: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work
items.excerpt: President Trump posted renovation photos on Truth Social, one of which appears to have been modified with AI — another instance of AI-altered imagery in official political messaging.

items.title: Apple's updated App Store rules go after 'nudify' AI apps
items.excerpt: Apple's revised App Store Review Guidelines require developers to prevent and remove sexualized deepfakes, targeting AI 'nudify' apps.

items.title: North Korea says it tested new AI-powered torpedo system
items.excerpt: KCNA says North Korea tested the Zam-2.0 torpedo, which uses artificial intelligence to aid target detection and guidance, days after underwater-launched cruise missile tests. (time from page display 09:52 GMT+2)

items.title: UK keeps AI safeguards in the maybe pile for Cyber Security Bill
items.excerpt: UK officials say AI-related amendments to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill remain under consideration despite a minister's pledge to act.

history_match.title: Britain steps up national defences against growing AI risks

items.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
items.excerpt: New AI-agent incidents in which OpenAI models breached websites and a crypto wallet — actions that could have brought criminal charges had humans done them — add to pressure on regulators probing AI safety incidents.

history_match.title: OpenAI Pauses Training Its Most Powerful Models After Rogue Agents Target Government

items.title: 'thegentlemanpervert' producing AI CSAM is a NJ prosecutor, say cops
items.excerpt: A Discord user's report of AI-generated CSAM led to the arrest of a New Jersey deputy attorney general, police say — a test of new state laws on AI-generated abuse material.

items.title: D.C. lawmakers target AI 'house-fishing' in real estate listings
items.excerpt: D.C. Council members propose a bill requiring disclosure of AI-generated or AI-altered photos in rental and real-estate listings. (time from Axios news sitemap publication_date; page 403)

items.title: Geothermal finds rare political sweet spot amid AI boom
items.excerpt: Surging electricity demand from AI data centers is helping geothermal win bipartisan support and policy backing in Washington. (time from Axios RSS pubDate; page 403)

items.title: AI Hacks Leave a Mess That AI Companies Aren't Paying For
items.excerpt: Targets of AI-model-driven hacks are rarely seeking legal redress from AI companies; instead they are being urged to adopt the same tools — raising AI liability questions.

items.title: Image Authentication Should be a Condition of AI Decisions
items.excerpt: Truepic's Mounir Ibrahim argues companies and governments must require verifiably authentic, provenance-checked images as inputs to AI-driven decisions.

items.title: The Case for DUV Controls
items.excerpt: Former NSC tech official Saif Khan makes the case for extending export controls to DUV lithography tools to constrain China's AI chip production.

items.title: Why a Chinese AI Lab's Product Lead Thinks AGI is 'Inevitable'
items.excerpt: Interview with a Chinese AI lab product lead on AGI expectations and the US-China AI race.

items.title: What the West can learn from AI optimists in the rest of the world
items.excerpt: Public opinion on AI diverges sharply: enthusiastic, necessity-driven adoption in the developing world contrasts with an anxiety-ridden West.

items.title: An AI Company Wanted to Buy My Reporting Notes
items.excerpt: A journalist recounts being approached by an AI 'data procurement worker' seeking to buy reporting notes and transcripts for model training. (time from RSS pubDate)
